strategies.overview: Facing RU with a stalwart expression, Quagsire is a decent physical wall, utilizing its ability Unaware to stonewall a vast majority of setup sweepers such as Bisharp, Gyarados, and Mimikyu. Quagsire uses Pokemon such as Bisharp and Mimikyu as opportunities to heal off chip damage or establish Spikes, while Toxic allows Quagsire to help hinder pesky foes immune to Earthquake like Noivern and Talonflame. Quagsire's main issue is that it fears most special attackers, as due to its poor special bulk, it is obliterated by Pokemon such as Basculegion-F, Ribombee, and Armarouge. Quagsire also immensely struggles with Grass-types such as Hisuian Lilligant and Amoonguss, as they can not only take its Earthquake but also hit it for 4x super effective damage. Grass-type coverage such as Wood Hammer from Mimikyu or Grass Knot from Jirachi can also OHKO Quagsire unexpectedly. Quagsire is also unable to effectively take on Pokemon such as Suicune with Unaware sets.
strategies.comments:
Other Options

Toxic Spikes can be used over Spikes in order to further spread poison by threatening Pokemon such as Suicune and Raikou that Quagsire does not want to directly switch into. Encore can be used to lock opposing Pokemon into status moves such as Roost and Recover, which can help Quagsire to spread Toxic, although it is prediction reliant because of Quagsire's low Speed. Whirlpool can be used to trap opposing Pokemon while dealing chip damage, allowing Quagsire to beat foes such as Tera Steel Flygon and Rotom-H it might otherwise not be able to touch. Stealth Rock can be used if there aren't any other Stealth Rock setters on the team. Body Press is an option on Quagsire to hit Bisharp a lot harder while also hitting Tera Steel Levitate Pokemon such as Flygon and Rotom-H it would otherwise struggle with. Counter can be used to surprise foes such as Galarian Zapdos and Mamoswine that think they can chip down Quagsire with their strong moves, dealing massive damage back to them. Rocky Helmet is an option on Quagsire in order to deal chip damage to Pokemon such as Galarian Zapdos and Maushold that it might otherwise be overwhelmed by. Water Absorb can be used over Unaware to help with matchups against Water-types such as Barraskewda and Suicune.

Checks and Counters

Special Wallbreakers: Due to Quagsire's low special bulk, wallbreakers like Gardevoir, Hisuian Goodra, and Volcanion threaten it immensely. Unaware can also hurt it, as it can ignore the Special Attack drops from moves such as Draco Meteor, meaning it can't even stay in on stat-lowered foes like Noivern.

Grass-types: Grass-types such as Hisuian Lilligant and Breloom threaten Quagsire with 4x super effective moves. Pokemon with Grass-type coverage such as Wood Hammer from Mimikyu and Grass Knot Jirachi can also annihilate Quagsire unexpectedly.

Toxic- and Ground-immune Foes: Toxic- and Ground-immune foes such as Gligar, Tera Steel Rotom-H, and Tera Steel Flygon can easily switch into Quagsire, as it cannot touch them back. This means they can either make progress with entry hazards in the case of Gligar or constantly chip Quagsire in the case of Rotom-H and Flygon, forcing Quagsire to use more Recovers.

Disruption Moves: Quagsire is extremely restricted by moves such as Taunt and Psychic Noise, as they mean it can't use Recover and potentially cannot use Spikes or Toxic, forcing it to either switch out or immediately use Earthquake, which Pokemon it can usually beat such as Galarian Zapdos and Talonflame can take advantage of. Quagsire is also vulnerable to Choice Scarf + Trick and Encore from Pokemon like Gardevoir and Maushold, which can lock it into a disadvantageous move.

movesets.name: Spikes
movesets.description:
Set Details

Toxic allows Quagsire to threaten Flying-types such as Galarian Zapdos, Noivern, and Gyarados while also helping wear down Pokemon such as Mamoswine and Hippowdon. Heavy-Duty Boots allows Quagsire to ignore chip damage from entry hazards that might otherwise overwhelm it, while Leftovers accentuates Quagsire's longevity by giving it passive healing. Unaware allows Quagsire to ignore offensive stat boosts from Pokemon such as Terrakion, Bisharp, and Rhyperior while also ignoring defensive stat boosts from Pokemon such as Registeel and Chesnaught in order to hit them harder, though it has the downside of ignoring stat drops such as the ones Hisuian Goodra's and Noivern's Draco Meteors cause. Tera Poison allows Quagsire to resist the Grass-type moves aimed at it from Pokemon such as Hisuian Lilligant and Breloom, helps it check Fighting-types such as Mienshao and Galarian Zapdos, makes its own Toxic 100% accurate, and allows it to become immune to Toxic from Umbreon and Amoonguss.

Quagsire fits best on bulky offense and balance teams, where it can be paired with other defensive Pokemon like Chesnaught and Chansey to help wall large amounts of the metagame. Wo-Chien pairs really well with Quagsire, as it can use Knock Off in order to help Quagsire's Spikes stacking while also switching into Pokemon such as Basculegion-F and Hisuian Goodra that threaten out Quagsire. In return, Quagsire can switch into Pokemon such as Entei and Galarian Zapdos that can threaten out Wo-Chien. Poison-immune Pokemon such as Amoonguss and Alolan Muk pair well with Quagsire, as they can not only take on the Grass-types such as Amoonguss and Hisuian Liligant that threaten it immensely but also take Toxic from Pokemon such as Umbreon and opposing Amoonguss, which Quagsire would otherwise have to Terastallize for. Specially defensive Pokemon such as Cyclizar, Chansey, and Umbreon pair well with Quagsire, as they can take on the special wallbreakers such as Reuniclus and Gengar that threaten it, while in return, Quagsire can take on Pokemon such as Bisharp and Mimikyu that threaten them. Wallbreakers such as Mamoswine and Armarouge appreciate Quagsire's chip damage helping wear down their checks. Stealth Rock setters such as Registeel and Jirachi can form entry hazard-stacking cores with Quagsire, which can heavily chip down foes.

movesets.name: Unaware Wall
movesets.description:
Quagsire is a notable physical wall thanks to its ability Unaware, which allows it to ignore boosts from setup sweepers like Salamence and Scizor. Toxic puts many notable Pokemon in the tier on a timer such as Hippowdon and Gastrodon. Quagsire ideally wants Spikes over Stealth Rock to force more chip damage on potential switch-ins; however, Stealth Rock is fine as an alternative if none of its other teammates can afford to fit it into their moveset. Alternatively, Ice Beam with a Relaxed nature allows Quagsire to 2HKO Hawlucha after Stealth Rock and lets it beat Substitute + Dragon Dance Tera Flying Tyranitars. The passive recovery of Leftovers allows Quagsire to check Choice Band Tyranitar and Mimikyu more easily; however, if the team can not fit entry hazard removal, Heavy-Duty Boots is much more appealing. Quagsire only uses Terastallization defensively to check certain dangerous offensive threats. Tera Poison grants Quagsire a perfectly accurate Toxic and a poison immunity while also allowing it to handle Grass-types and offensive threats that use Grass-type moves such as Tsareena, Trailblaze Scizor, and Seed Bomb Pawmot. Tera Ghost allows Quagsire to beat Maushold by becoming immune to Population Bomb as well as check Slither Wing and Lucario more easily. Tera Ghost also has the added benefit of letting Quagsire serve as a spinblocker against spinners such as Tsareena.

Quagsire primarily fits on balance, stall, and bulky offense teams as a defensive glue that holds these teams together. Common teammates for Quagsire include Stealth Rock setters such as Tinkaton and Tyranitar, which can allow Quagsire to run Spikes. Both can check Gengar, special Salamence, and Iron Jugulis, which pose a threat to Quagsire. Tinkaton can also use Knock Off on Heavy-Duty Boots users such as Sticky Hold Gastrodon, Scream Tail, and Wo-Chien to rack up more damage from Quagsire's Spikes. Scream Tail is another Pokemon that complements Quagsire, as it is able to handle special Salamence as well as Gallade, while Quagsire is able to keep Bisharp and non-Trailblaze Scizor in check. Talonflame is another ideal partner for Quagsire as it can check Tsareena and Giga Drain variants of Wo-Chien. Blissey on stall teams is also a strong partner for Quagsire by virtue of walling almost every special attacker in the tier such as Iron Jugulis, Noivern, and Sandy Shocks.

strategies.comments:
Other Options

(Ground)

Ice Beam threatens Gliscor, which does not fear Toxic, and Landorus-T utilizing Taunt or Substitute, which prevents Quagsire from inflicting it with Toxic poison; however, these matchups are specific and other teammates can handle them, letting Quagsire retain its useful utility moves. Body Press may be used to better check Roaring Moon, Hisuian Samurott, Cetitan, and Weavile, but the damage discrepancy with Earthquake is minimal, and Earthquake will do more damage in most other matchups.

movesets.name: Unaware Wall (Ground)
movesets.description:
Quagsire is a great option for Ground teams due to its physical bulk and Unaware, checking a wide range of physical attackers like Hisuian Samurott, Cetitan, and Choice Scarf Urshifu-R. Stealth Rock or Spikes wears down threats like Greninja, Iron Valiant, and Meowscarada. Toxic allows Quagsire to further wither down opponents alongside the entry hazards, notably putting Dragonite, Ting-Lu, and Great Tusk on a timer. Leftovers grants Quagsire passive recovery, improving its longevity and ability to repeatedly take hits more reliably. Meanwhile, Heavy-Duty Boots prevents detrimental entry hazards from wearing it down, allowing it to freely pivot. Rocky Helmet punishes multi-hit moves such as Urshifu-R's Surging Strikes and Weavile's Triple Axel as well as Roaring Moon, Hisuian Samurott, and Cinderace attempting to pivot.

Quagsire's ability to wall setup sweepers like Dragonite and Ceruledge is heavily appreciated by its teammates. Water Absorb Clodsire switches into attacks from Greninja, Walking Wake, and Ogerpon-W while also contributing to entry hazard stacking via Toxic Spikes. Iron Treads removes entry hazards with Rapid Spin should Quagsire forgo Heavy-Duty Boots and checks Fairy-types like Hatterene and Flutter Mane. Great Tusk, Garchomp, and Landorus value Quagsire's entry hazards, which aid in their wallbreaking. Choice Scarf Great Tusk checks Choice Specs Flutter Mane, Greninja, and Hoopa-U while removing held items from Mandibuzz, Brambleghast, and Tornadus-T to make them more susceptible to Quagsire's entry hazards. Garchomp threatens Steel-types like Corviknight, Skarmory, and Air Balloon Gholdengo with its Fire-type coverage. Landorus checks the Ogerpon formes with Sludge Wave when using a Choice Scarf set and can utilize Rock Slide to catch Volcarona and Moltres off-guard. Ting-Lu and Quagsire make a great entry hazard-stacking core, as Ting-Lu is able to phaze opponents out with Whirlwind as well as check special attackers such as Latios, Gholdengo, and Raging Bolt. Mamoswine appreciates Quagsire's entry hazards; in return, it can fend off Ice-types such as Alolan Ninetales and Articuno while also threatening Meowscarada, Enamorus, Gliscor, and Landorus. Gliscor aids in setting up entry hazards and spreading Toxic poison while also being able to switch into opposing Toxic for Quagsire. Additionally, Gliscor provides Knock Off support to better accentuate the team's entry hazard setting while threatening opposing Gliscor and Gholdengo with its Swords Dance set.

movesets.name: Unaware Wall (Water)
movesets.description:
Quagsire is a decent choice on Water teams thanks to its good bulk, access to Recover, useful typing, and ability to get Spikes up against threats that it walls, like Iron Defense + Body Press Zamazenta, Dragon Dance Roaring Moon, and Iron Hands. Toxic lets Quagsire force progress on defensive Pokemon and offensive switch-ins such as Meowscarada, Latios, and the Ogerpon formes, which in conjunction with Spikes racks up a significant amount of chip damage on opposing teams over time. Spikes can wear down threatening special attackers that force out Quagsire like Ursaluna-BM and Choice Specs Flutter Mane. Alternatively, Stealth Rock can be run if Quagsire has no teammates setting it up. Heavy-Duty Boots lets Quagsire ignore treacherous entry hazards such as Spikes and Toxic Spikes, which can easily wear it down over the course of a game. Leftovers let Quagsire passively regenerate HP, which can help it conserve Recover PP. Alternatively, Rocky Helmet lets Quagsire punish common physical attacks, such as IronPress Zamazenta's Body Press and Choice Scarf Roaring Moon's U-turn, and wear down said opponents over time in conjunction with Toxic and Spikes.

Toxapex is a good teammate for Quagsire, as it complements Quagsire's defensive typing well, being able to take on Grass-types like Meowscarada while Quagsire handles Electric-types like Iron Hands. Ogerpon-W and Greninja appreciate Quagsire giving them extra chip damage to force progress against answers like Archaludon and Iron Hands, respectively, with Spikes. Primarina and Keldeo appreciate Quagsire being able to scare off Poison-types like Alolan Muk, allowing them to set up, while Spikes forces very handy damage onto their answers. In return, Keldeo can take on Kingambit and Chien-Pao, two physical attackers that can overpower Quagsire, while Primarina can switch in on Dragon-types like special attacking Dragapult. Empoleon provides a nice Grass neutrality and Fairy resistance to the team, letting it take on threats like Hydrapple and Hatterene, alongside being a specially defensive tank that pairs nicely with Quagsire's Electric immunity and physical bulk. It also sets up Stealth Rock to form an entry hazard-stacking core alongside Quagsire.

strategies.overview:
Draft Order: Round 7 onwards

Price Range: 5-6 points

Overview: Reliable recovery, multiple entry hazards, an amazing defensive typing, and two great defensive abilities make Quagsire seem like a fantastic wall that can effectively deal with many physical setup sweepers. Unfortunately, its crippling weakness to Grass-type moves and Freeze-Dry as well as its passivity can hold it back against foes with coverage or moves like Taunt. Quagsires's access to Stealth Rock, Spikes, and Toxic Spikes allows it to be an competent hazard setter in most matchups, and Unaware enables it to check and disrupt many physical setup sweepers despite its mediocre stats.
strategies.comments:
Common Roles

Unaware Wall: Setup sweepers without Grass-type coverage or Freeze-Dry can often be walled by Quagsire through Unaware, since it can use Recover to stay healthy enough to deal with them. It can also use these opportunities to set its entry hazard of choice or spread status. Quagsire's low stats require it to invest heavily to deal with either physical or special attackers, and it generally is only able to deal with one of the two.

Defensive Utility: If Quagsire is needed to check Water-type attackers or block Flip Turn, forgoing Unaware for Water Absorb can be effectivewhile still using similar utility moves. Passing on Unaware makes it susceptible to setup sweepers, giving the Water-types it is meant to check even more options to get around it, and most high-tier Water-types also have Grass-type coverage.

Common Moves

Primary STAB Moves: Earthquake, Liquidation, Earth Power, Surf, High Horsepower

Setup Moves: Curse

Utility Moves: Stealth Rock, Spikes, Toxic Spikes, Recover, Toxic, Yawn, Encore, Haze, Seismic Toss

Coverage: Ice Beam, Ice Punch, Sludge Bomb, Body Press, Stone Edge, Iron Tail

Niche Moves

Whirlpool: Whirlpool can be effective at trapping and damaging foe over time, especially ones that resist Quagsire's STAB movesand are immune to Toxic.

Counter: Sets with Counter can achieve surprise OHKOs on physical attackers, pairing well with Rindo Berry.

Bulldoze / Icy Wind / Rock Tomb: Lowering the Speed of foes with Bulldoze, Icy Wind, or Rock Tomb can allow Quagsire's partners to deal with faster foes that can beat it.

Common Items

Leftovers: Quagsire often stays in for multiple turns, making the healing from Leftovers over time highly useful.

Rocky Helmet: Rocky Helmet allows Quagsire to provide even more chip damage against foes with contact moves, helping it beat the physical attackers that it is often expected to check.

Heavy-Duty Boots: Despite Quagsire's resistance to Stealth Rock, it is susceptible to being chipped down by Spikes and Toxic Spikes, making Heavy-Duty Boots a good option.

Niche Items

Resistance Berries: Quagsire's crippling weakness to Grass-type attacks and Freeze-Dry can be mitigated for one turn with Rindo Berry or Yache Berry, respectively, allowing it to deal with certain foes with coverage through Toxic or Counter.

Mental Herb: Quagsire's low Speed and passivity makes it especially susceptible to Taunt and Encore. Mental Herb can allow it to set entry hazards or use Recover for one turn against these moves.

Eject Button: To maintain momentum against wallbreakers or on pivot moves like U-turn that can chip Quagsire down easily, Eject Button can be used.

Tera

Quagsire should not be a Tera Captain, as it removes one of its main strengths in its great defensive typing while not providing much advantage to it. If Quagsire is a Tera Captain, it can defensively Terastallize into Grass-resistant types like Tera Steel and Poison. Tera Fire can also be combined with Water Absorb to remove its weakness to Water along with resisting Grass.

Draft Strategy

Quagsire fits well on balanced or more defensive drafts, dealing with opposing setup sweepers while setting entry hazards or spreading status. Access to Stealth Rock, Spikes, and Toxic Spikes gives these types of drafts many options for setting hazards, making longer games more effective. This makes Quagsire a good late addition to many defensive cores, adding only one weakness with two possible immunities.

Grass-resistant Pokemon: Quagsire is often threatened out by foes with Grass-type moves. Partners like Tornadus-T, Gouging Fire, and Scizor are effective at switching into these moves and taking advantage of the status effects or entry hazards that itprovides.

Spinblockers: Quagsire can set its entry hazards of choice multiple times a match, and having spinblockers like Gholdengo, Annihilape and Pecharunt can allow it to keep them on the field.

Offensive Partners: Having many entry hazards at its disposal along with Toxic can allow Quagsire to soften opposing walls for its team. This support allows partners like Iron Valiant, Kingambit, and Iron Boulder to break through the opponent's team more effectively.

Checks and Counters

Grass-type Attacks: Quagsire's crippling weakness to Grass-type moves allows foes like Ogerpon-W and Meowscarada to easily OKHO it. Even weaker non-STAB attacks from Pokemon like Volcarona and Manaphy are also able to comfortably break through it.

Taunt / Encore: Quagsire relies on Recover, entry hazards, and Toxic to be effective. Foes that can disrupt these moves though Taunt and Encore can prevent it from dealing with setup sweepers or providing hazards for its team.

Wallbreakers: With Quagsire's mediocre defensive stats, strong wallbreakers—especially special attackers—including Latios, Iron Bundle, and Urshifu-S are able to muscle through it, even more so if opposing entry hazards are up.

Chip Damage: Quagsire is quite susceptible to chip damage from entry hazards and status, which necessitates repeated use of Recover, giving frequent opportunities to the opponent. Limited Recover PP can lead to it being unable to deal with certain threats in the long term, especially foes that can sustain their health.

movesets.name: Unaware Wall
movesets.description: Quagsire is an excellent wall and entry hazard setter in Ubers UU, as it has Unaware, a solid defensive typing, and a vast utility movepool, allowing it to check setup sweepers like Roaring Moon and Zacian. Spikes, Stealth Rock, and Toxic Spikes allow Quagsire to support its team with hazards, reducing the team's passivity and forcing chip damage on key threats like Palkia-O and Ogerpon-H. Toxic allows Quagsire to put opposing threats such as Zacian and Great Tusk on a timer. Unaware allows Quagsire to stifle setup sweepers like Swords Dance Zacian and Dragon Dance Arceus-Poison while also allowing it to handle Nasty Plot Mewtwo fairly well. Tera Poison allows Quagsire to handle Fairy- and Grass-type attacks from Pokemon like Zacian and Arceus-Grass, respectively, while also keeping it safe from Poison. Quagsire appreciates help from special walls like Blissey and specially defensive Magearna, as they can patch up its weaker Special Defense, and they fit well alongside it on stall and balance teams, handling threats like Arceus-Dark, Palkia-O, and Dialga. Dragon- and Steel-types like Arceus-Dragon and Skarmory also pair well with Quagsire, as they can relieve it of entry hazard setting duty while also switching in on Grass-types like Rillaboom and Ogerpon formes. Quagsire enables offensive threats like Zacian, Arceus-Poison, and Deoxys with its hazard setting, putting their checks, such as Arceus-Poison and Giratina, into KO range of their attacks.
